title: fix(arcs): a bore at a STEP hole's own size posts clean - mesh, arc fit and arc reading share the gouge verdict
body:
## What changed

A Bore at a STEP hole's own size was refused by the program gate as a 20 mm gouge. The STEP mesh's chord sagitta on the Ø25 wall (0.022 mm) was larger than the gouge verdict (0.01 mm). Capping the mesh exposed two more places where the full verdict budget was being spent:

1. **STEP chord cap** (`app::geometry::import::step`). The chord target is now `min(extent/1000, DEV_TOL/2)` = 0.005 mm at most. This is mkinney's held commit from `mkinney:issue/689-bore-sagitta`, cherry-picked with authorship kept, together with his `bore_facet_sagitta` test and decision file. Credit to his investigation on the issue.
2. **Arc fit vertex share** (`motion::machining2d::arcs`, `ARC_FIT_VERTEX_SHARE = 0.5`). Every vertex an arc replaces must stand within `tol/2` of the fitted circle. The chord-hug test keeps the full `tol`.
3. **Closed-ring orientation** (same file). A run whose ends meet within `tol` takes its turning direction from its signed area, no longer from the anchor triple. On a regular rim the two quarter-turn anchors tie, and the one picked lies before the pivot, so the triple read the ring backwards. As a result every closed rim ended on a chord. On the Ø25 hole that kinked the seam tangent, and the lead-out crossed the ring (9 `Crossing` findings in solid_law once the gouges were gone).
4. **Law (b) reads arc moves at `gouge_tol/4`** (`sim::verify::section`, `ARC_READ_SHARE = 0.25`). Before, the law read an arc by its inscribed chords at the full gouge tolerance (0.01 mm); it now reads them at 0.0025 mm. No limit moved: the floor `r - leave - tol`, `GOUGE_TOL`, `DEV_TOL`, endpoint containment, `wall_gouge` and the solid-law allowance are all unchanged.

   **This change flips verdicts in both directions.**
   - **A former gouge now passes:** a nominal arc round a convex wall. Example: the r = 5 cutter's centre on r = 34.998 round an r = 30 island has a true clearance of 4.998 mm against a 4.99 mm floor. The old chords sagged about 0.0099 mm toward the island, read 4.988 and convicted it. The quarter reading reads at least 4.9955 and passes it. Below the chord clamp the quarter reading stands within 2.5 µm of the arc. `MAX_ARC_CHORDS` (1024) binds for a full circle above r ~ 531 mm (about `531 · (2π/θ)²` mm for a sweep θ; the old reading hit it above r ~ 2125 mm). Above that radius the reading degrades toward the old one, never past it: it takes at least as many chords, and its worst sagitta is never larger. This is pinned by `verify_arc_reading::the_quarter_reading_is_never_coarser_than_the_old_one_at_any_radius`. The pass is the correct verdict, because the cut arc honours the floor. This is what cleared the 4 shoulder_adaptive gouges and the 0.010-0.012 mm solid_law gouges.
   - **A former pass is now a gouge:** an arc bowing past the floor into a wall. Example: an r = 20 arc whose apex stands 5 µm past the r = 4 cutter's floor at a straight wall. The old 5-chord reading put the apex mid-chord, 0.0096 mm low, and passed a real gouge. The quarter reading convicts it.
   - **Both flips are pinned** in the new `crates/app/tests/verify_arc_reading.rs`, with the analytic distance asserted. With `ARC_READ_SHARE` set back to 1.0, exactly the two flip tests fail; I checked this locally. Arcs cut 15 µm past the floor round a convex wall and inside a concave wall are convicted under both readings, so the concave side is at least as strict as before. Plasma verdicts are unaffected: the plasma laws (`sim::verify::plasma`) never call law (b), and `plasma_laws`, `plasma_profile`, `plasma_post`, `plasma_post_refusals` and `plasma_machine` pass on the merged tree.
5. `lead_in`/`lead_out` moved to `arc_leads.rs` to keep `arcs.rs` under 400 lines. This is structure only, and the file has a provenance line naming the public source of the lead shapes.

The decisions, including the options dropped (verdict slack, mesh-only tuning, a side-aware fit), the verdict flip and the STEP timing are in `docs/decisions/689-step-chord-cap.md`.

## Readings

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Milling-test.step facets / import (debug) | 448, ~14 ms | 952, ~27 ms |
| sample_ap214.step (largest STEP in testdata) | 1550, ~81 ms | 1550, ~64 ms (unchanged mesh) |
| Ø25 wall chord sagitta | 0.022 mm | ≤ 0.005 mm |
| Nominal bore, program gate | gouge, 20.00 mm | clean |
| Bore 0.05 mm oversize | - | refused (`gouge:`) |
| solid_law R35 arc centre (fit) | (0.027, -0.040), r 34.958 | (0.004, -0.006), r 34.993 |
| solid_law contour with cap only | 10 Gouge (0.010-0.012 mm) | 0 |
| Ø25 hole ring (R7.498) | 2 arcs + a 3.2° chord at the seam | 3 arcs about (0, 0) |

**Huge models.** The facet budget bounds the mesh:
- Refinement passes run only while the mesh is at most `budget / 8` (`MAX_FACETS` = 30 M, less what earlier shells used).
- A pass at most quadruples the count, so a kept mesh stays under about `budget / 2` (15 M).
- A triangulation past the budget is dropped and the last mesh is kept.
- There are at most 24 passes.

**An over-budget model, both directions.** A model that hits the budget stops short of the 0.005 mm target. It keeps a mesh coarser than the cap and only logs "reduced fidelity" to stderr. The facets are chords inscribed in the true surface, so the error cuts both ways:
- **Concave wall:** the facets stand toward the tool, and a nominal finish can read as a false gouge. This is the safe side.
- **Convex wall:** the facets sit inside the true surface, so the mesh wall looks farther from the tool than the real wall is. A real gouge, up to the model's actual chord error, can pass. This is the unsafe side.

This PR does not introduce that risk. I verified this in `step.rs`:
- Before #689 the target was `extent/1000`, and the refinement passes (start `extent/4`, halve, clamp at the target) were the same.
- The new target is never larger than the old one. Up to the old target the pass sequence is identical, and the budget stop is the same check on the same meshes.
- So every STEP mesh is now at least as fine as it was before, for every model.

This PR removes the risk for every model that fits the budget. For an over-budget model it remains. **The over-budget case is tracked in #864.**

## Pinning tests

- `bore_facet_sagitta::a_bore_at_the_step_holes_own_size_passes_the_gate`
- `bore_facet_sagitta::a_bore_cut_oversize_into_the_same_wall_is_still_refused`
- `arcs::a_fitted_arc_keeps_every_vertex_within_half_the_tolerance`
- `arcs::a_closed_rim_fits_whole_in_either_direction`
- `verify_arc_reading::a_nominal_arc_round_a_convex_wall_passes_where_the_old_chords_convicted_it`
- `verify_arc_reading::an_arc_cut_past_the_floor_round_a_convex_wall_is_convicted`
- `verify_arc_reading::an_arc_cut_past_the_floor_inside_a_concave_wall_is_convicted`
- `verify_arc_reading::an_arc_bowing_past_the_floor_into_a_straight_wall_is_convicted_where_the_old_chords_hid_it`
- `verify_arc_reading::the_quarter_reading_is_never_coarser_than_the_old_one_at_any_radius` (review round 2)
- The five Milling-test.step suites stay clean with the cap on: `solid_law`, `lead_approach`, `level_links`, `wall_arc_entry`, `shoulder_adaptive`. All five failed with the cap alone.

## Goldens moved

Each golden batch is in its own commit: cd5c3885, 2ff63c70, 18c30494. Every move comes from the arc fit; none comes from a generator change. Figures are re-measured from the diffs.

- **`contour_disc_hole.cl` and `contour_tangential_lead.cl`** (R6 bore, r = 3 ring):
  - The closed rim now closes on arcs: per level, a Feed plus two arcs become three arcs about (20, 10).
  - The lead-out leaves on the true tangent. Its end moves **2.12 mm**, from (18.390, 8.541) to (17.004, 10.148). The earlier "1.4 mm" was the X component only.
  - The lead-out radius goes from 1.5 to 3 mm. The old lead was shrunk against the kinked chord tangent.
- **`contour_bore_arc_entry.cl`** (R12 bore): the trailing Feed becomes an arc. The lead-out end moves from (16.927, 3.926) to (17.000, 4.001), **0.10 mm**.
- **`finish3d_{contour,ramp_parallel,scallop,spiral}_plateau.cl`**: one corner arc per side had vertices past half the budget. It splits into a feed plus an arc. That arc's centre moves from (9.663, 9.851) to (9.958, 9.962), **0.31 mm** closer to the true corner centre (10, 10). +3 Feed per file.
- **`finish3d_project_dome.cl`, `finish3d_radial_dome.cl`**: ring arcs past the vertex share stay chords (+110 Feed, -4 Arc). Chords are the verified polygon.
- **`finish3d_waterline_cone.cl`**: closed rings fit whole (-17 Feed, +4 Arc).
- **`nc/{fanuc,carvera,haas,heidenhain,mazak,sinumerik,tormach,doosan-dnm}/contour_{disc_hole,tangential_lead}.nc`**: the regenerated CL above, posted. Doosan DNM merged after the first round; its diff is byte-for-byte the Fanuc body diff.

I checked what main gained since the first round, up to 72ab8fdb. Only the Doosan DNM contour goldens moved, and only from the arc fit. The trochoidal slot, plasma laws and post, microARC, fixture plates and mod vises moved no golden. Their suites, and every other gated golden suite, pass on the merged tree; I did not single out the PathPilot lathe and fixture-routing suites beyond the full quick gate.

## Test expectations changed (not loosened)

- **`wall_arc_entry`**:
  - On the capped mesh a proved arc fits beside the bore wall. The test pins **exactly 5** bore entries, one per bore level, each landing on a bore level, and **8** plunges (5 outer + 3 bore levels past the second, no grazes).
  - Verifier silence (`warnings == 0`: no gouge, no crossing) is still asserted.
  - The seam check `!notes.contains("kept as planned")` asserts that no crossing pair is left. The seam law writes that note only when it could not part a crossing.
- **`solid_law_goldens`**: the R6 bore's r = 3 ring and its 3 mm leads share one circle, so the program was and stays refused by law (a). More crossing pairs are recorded (6 and 12), with the same refusal. This predates the PR; the reviewer's note that a refused program has posted NC goldens is worth a separate issue.
- **`shoulder_adaptive`**: the recess check reads arc moves along their arc. Before, it read them as the straight line from `from` to `to`.

## Gate (tree: this branch merged with origin/main 72ab8fdb; head bb71d19d)

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, in full on this head: green, 45.1 min: sim lib ok (31 s), motion suites ok (467 s, `trochoid_slot` included), app suites ok (2205 s, 263 binaries, including `verify_arc_reading`, `conformance`, `trochoid_op`, `microarc_test_part`, `plasma_gate`, `plasma_post`, `plasma_post_refusals`, `plasma_profile` and `plasma_machine`). Every sim test binary was also run (`cargo test -p camcraft-sim --tests`, `plasma_laws` included): 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

- **Review round 2** (commit after bb71d19d, test and docs only): `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test verify_arc_reading` passed 5/5 and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The full quick gate was green on bb71d19d; a test-only addition does not need it again.

## Not exercised

- No batch or release tier was run, and no `--ignored` heavy lanes.
- The UI crate was not run (untouched by this PR).
- The bore on EM-0800-4FL and EM-0600-4FL from the issue was not pinned separately; it is the same wall.
- STL/OBJ imports keep whatever chord error the file carries.
- No STEP model larger than sample_ap214.step (100 KB) exists in testdata. The huge-model behaviour above is read from the code, not timed.

Changelog: A bore at a STEP hole's own size posts clean: STEP meshes are capped at 0.005 mm chord error, arc fitting keeps vertices within half the tolerance, closed rings fit whole, and the gouge law reads arcs at a quarter of its tolerance (a nominal arc round a convex wall now passes; an arc bowing past the floor between its old chord joints is now caught) (#689)

Effort: high (no escalation; one review round)

Fixes #689
